body: The new property names should use underscores instead of slashes, like other engine properties. Otherwise, they can't be referenced from GDScript without using `set()`.

Increase precision for duration values:

```suggestion
	ADD_PROPERTYI(PropertyInfo(Variant::FLOAT, "animation/duration", PROPERTY_HINT_RANGE, "0,1,0.001,or_less,or_greater"), "set_animation_duration", "get_animation_duration", PHASE_NORMAL);
```

Snapping animation durations to a frame count to a 60 Hz display can lead to better visuals (e.g. `0.067` for a transition that lasts 4 frames on a 60 Hz display). Here, being able to specify values down to the nearest millisecond can help.

body:
Yeah this could probably done differently. But basically internally, Trees, ItemLists, and TabBars have IDs like "item:0", "item:1", "item:2" etc. This lets you override that, so every item would have the same ID, and would animate into each other rather than as separate items. The main reason is it allows sliding items, because they have the same animation id, like this

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/56bb1e80-2e19-44ce-ba10-16bced8b7ae9


But honestly, its maybe better to just have flags on Tree TabBar and ItemList like "use_sliding_animation" or something
